ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — History and Physical — Rabindranath Tagore

code.originalText: New-patient visit for a weak stream, straining, and frequent urination at night, with a feeling that the bladder does not empty

text.paragraph: New-patient visit for a weak stream, straining, and frequent urination at night, with a feeling that the bladder does not empty [S]
This fictional modern episode addresses the presenting concerns below. [S]

list.item: A weak stream, straining, dribbling, and getting up four times a night for months; lately he passes only small amounts and feels his bladder never empties. [S]
Since a severe urinary infection in the hills five months ago he has not felt well; he wants to keep writing and teaching. [S]
He fears an operation more than he fears his illness, and wants to know every gentler choice before any surgery is decided. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Rabindranath Tagore was born on 7 May 1861 in the Jorasanko mansion in Calcutta, the youngest son of Debendranath Tagore, a leader of the Brahmo Samaj; the name Tagore is the anglicised transliteration of Thakur. [D]

He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 "because of his profoundly sensitive, fresh and beautiful verse, by which, with consummate skill, he has made his poetic thought, expressed in his own English words, a part of the literature of the West". [D]
He started a school at Santiniketan that began formally on 22 December 1901 with five students, and around it he built Visva-Bharati, an unconventional university. [D]
He was known by the sobriquets Gurudeb, Kobiguru, and Bishwokobi. [D]

His last five years were marked by chronic pain and two long periods of illness: in late 1937 he lost consciousness and remained comatose and near death for a time, and in late 1940 a similar spell followed, from which he never recovered. [D]

On 15 September 1940, while visiting Kalimpong, he fell seriously ill with severe pain in his lower abdomen; doctors diagnosed a severe urinary tract infection, and he was brought back, unconscious, to Calcutta. [D]
In the last two years of his life illness confined him to the house, with swollen feet, numbness of the fingers, and frequent fevers; women of his family and household nursed him at home. [D]

He sought cure in allopathy, homeopathy, and ayurvedic medicine; physicians including Bidhan Chandra Roy and Nilratan Sarkar supervised his treatment; he is reported to have refused surgery despite repeated insistence from his doctors, to have sought a herbal cure, and to have said that he was more afraid of complicated medical treatment than of death. [D]
He suffered the untimely deaths of his wife and three of his children; he took his daughter Renuka to hill stations in the Himalayas for her recovery from tuberculosis. [D]

tr.td: Urinary retention with severe lower urinary tract symptoms (bladder scan 640 mL after voiding) and a raised creatinine, cause under evaluation
S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the diagnosis of benign prostatic hyperplasia with chronic retention at the two-week visit.

list.item: Urinary retention with severe lower urinary tract symptoms (bladder scan 640 mL after voiding) and a raised creatinine, cause under evaluation: active, confirmed [S]

Evaluation: IPSS with the quality-of-life question, bladder scan for post-void residual, urinalysis and urine culture, blood count, creatinine and electrolytes, digital rectal examination, and a kidney and bladder ultrasound for obstruction; a frequency-volume chart once voiding. Guideline: Management of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Attributed to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: AUA Guideline, Part I (Initial Work-up and Medical Management) and Part II (Surgical Evaluation and Treatment) (2021); AUA White Paper on Nonneurogenic Chronic Urinary Retention: Consensus Definition, Treatment Algorithm, and Outcome End Points (2017); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, Benign prostatic hyperplasia monograph (2026) [S]

PSA only after shared decision-making: it helps estimate prostate size and choose treatment; screening for prostate cancer is not recommended at his age, and he would not want treatment for a slow-growing cancer; drawn before the catheter is placed, because retention and catheters raise it. Guideline: Management of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Attributed to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: AUA Guideline, Part I (Initial Work-up and Medical Management) and Part II (Surgical Evaluation and Treatment) (2021); Prostate Cancer: Screening (2018); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, Benign prostatic hyperplasia monograph (2026) [S]

Indwelling urethral catheter to drain the bladder, with a closed drainage system, the bag below the bladder, daily washing with soap and water, no routine antibiotics or bladder washouts, no treatment of bacteria in the urine without symptoms, a change every four weeks, and same-day review for fever, pain, blood, or a blocked catheter. Guideline: AUA White Paper on Nonneurogenic Chronic Urinary Retention: Consensus Definition, Treatment Algorithm, and Outcome End Points (2017); Diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of catheter-associated urinary tract infection in adults: 2009 International Clinical Practice Guidelines from the Infectious Diseases Society of America (2009) [S]

Tamsulosin 0.4 mg at bedtime for at least three days and usually several weeks before a trial without catheter; fall precautions: take it after the evening meal, rise slowly, sit to pass urine at night, and use a night light. Guideline: Management of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Attributed to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: AUA Guideline, Part I (Initial Work-up and Medical Management) and Part II (Surgical Evaluation and Treatment) (2021); American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults (2023) [S]

Urology consultation for chronic urinary retention with a raised creatinine: confirm the cause, judge the risk, plan the trial without catheter, advise on a 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor, and set out the procedures that suit a frail 79-year-old who wants to avoid an operation. Guideline: Management of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Attributed to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: AUA Guideline, Part I (Initial Work-up and Medical Management) and Part II (Surgical Evaluation and Treatment) (2021); Management of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Attributed to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH): AUA Guideline Amendment 2023 (2023); AUA White Paper on Nonneurogenic Chronic Urinary Retention: Consensus Definition, Treatment Algorithm, and Outcome End Points (2017); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, Benign prostatic hyperplasia monograph (2026) [S]

Medication review with the AGS Beers Criteria: avoid anticholinergic drugs for bladder symptoms while in retention, first-generation antihistamines, and benzodiazepines; avoid nonselective alpha-blockers; review his herbal preparation with the pharmacist for interactions and unlabeled ingredients. Guideline: American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults (2023); Lead, mercury, and arsenic in US- and Indian-manufactured Ayurvedic medicines sold via the Internet (2008) [S]

Monitor on the CMID and AUA schedule: IPSS at every visit once voiding; post-void residual with each trial without catheter and after it; creatinine with retention; PSA at baseline and six months after starting finasteride, doubled for interpretation; response to tamsulosin at four to twelve weeks and to finasteride at three to six months. Guideline: Management of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Attributed to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: AUA Guideline, Part I (Initial Work-up and Medical Management) and Part II (Surgical Evaluation and Treatment) (2021); Management of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Attributed to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH): AUA Guideline Amendment 2023 (2023); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, Benign prostatic hyperplasia monograph (2026) [S]

Geriatric assessment before any surgical decision: frailty, gait and falls, orthostatic blood pressure on tamsulosin, cognition, mood, delirium risk, nutrition, and what matters most to him. Guideline: Management of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Attributed to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: AUA Guideline, Part I (Initial Work-up and Medical Management) and Part II (Surgical Evaluation and Treatment) (2021); American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults (2023) [S]
